t: Nader Shah, a general from the Afshar tribe, expelled Iran's occupiers and crowned himself Shah in 1736.
His 1739 sack of Delhi crippled the Mughal Empire and brought the Peacock Throne and Koh-i-Noor to Persia.
Built on one man's military genius, the empire shattered within months of his assassination in 1747.
dyk: The treasure Nader Shah took from Delhi in 1739 was so vast that he remitted taxes throughout Iran for three years.
ev: Nader expels the Ghilzai Afghans from Isfahan after seven years of occupation
Nader is proclaimed Shah after a great assembly on the Mughan plain
Nader crushes a much larger Mughal army at Karnal and enters Delhi
Nader campaigns in Central Asia, subduing Bukhara and Khiva
Nader has his eldest son Reza Qoli blinded on suspicion of plotting
Nader defeats the Ottomans at Kars
Nader Shah is assassinated by his own officers near Quchan
Agha Mohammad Khan Qajar takes Mashhad; Shahrokh dies, ending the dynasty
